label: rem:observability-independent-motivation
title: Independent motivation for observability: why $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0$ is not an NS assumption
html:
Does the QOU observability axiom \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 stand independently, or does it merely smuggle in a Navier--Stokes blowup conclusion?

The axiom carries five structural motivations independent of Navier--Stokes. A sixth, contact non-integrability, is withdrawn (item 2).

1. Gauge irreducibility. Within the archimedean realisation, observability translates to H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) = 0: the gauge connection A must be irreducible (no nonzero gauge-equivariant sections inhabit the adjoint bundle). Irreducibility is the standard generic condition governing connections over compact manifolds. Reducible connections collapse onto a lower-dimensional stratum. This serves as a core gauge-theory condition (Donaldson, Uhlenbeck, Atiyah--Bott) decades older than QOU.

2. Contact non-integrability (withdrawn). This item formerly identified observability with non-degeneracy of a Levi form. That identification is withdrawn. The chapter's plane field lives on the three-dimensional flow domain, where its Levi datum is the single scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi of the vorticity direction \xi (core Levi form). No result in the corpus links that scalar to \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0.

3. Tannaka--Krein reconstruction. The fibre functor \tau reconstructs A as a functional Hopf algebra using Tannaka--Krein duality. For this algebra to survive as a quantum group (avoiding degeneration into a quantum groupoid), its representation category must be semisimple. Observability ensures the adjoint representation remains simple (rejecting any trivial sub-representation), a strict requirement for \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) semisimplicity.

4. Mass non-degeneracy. The mass identity m \propto \oint_\varrho \|\nabla_A q\| \cdot \|L \wedge F^+\| yields a nonzero value for a stable vortex \varrho strictly when L \neq 0 at the vortex points. If observability drops at \varrho, L \to 0 and m \to 0: the vortex becomes physically massless, reduced to a gauge artifact.

5. Particle existence. The SU(2) emergence theorem requires observability to extract the gauge group \mathrm{SU}(2) from the QOU axioms. Stripping observability collapses the gauge group to a lesser subgroup (e.g., \mathrm{U}(1)). The stunted representation theory fails to produce the complete particle spectrum: hadronic physics vanishes.

6. Measurability. The descriptor "observable" is absolute: every internal degree of freedom of A responds to measurement through the fibre functor \tau. A non-trivial morphism \phi \colon \mathbf{1} \to \mathrm{Ad}(A) would introduce a hidden symmetry immune to measurement, hiding a sector of the universe from physical observation.

Consequences of dropping observability.

A quantum pre-universe (QPU) satisfies all QOU axioms except observability. In a QPU:

The QPU supplies a fundamentally weaker framework, and it permits NS regularity.

The relationship between observability and NS.

The logic proceeds strictly one way:

  \text{Observability} \Longrightarrow \text{NS singular}

The converse fails. Classical NS blowup could trigger without observability via entirely unrelated PDE mechanics; conversely, categorical NS-regularity (\mathrm{NS}(A) = e(\xi) = 0, \chi(A) = 0) fits within a QPU. Within the QOU model, the observability axiom encodes a measurement principle spanning gauge theory, geometry, and representation theory, from which \mathrm{NS}(A) = e(\xi) \neq 0 follows as a downstream topological consequence; identifying that internal class with classical 3D PDE blowup is the separate model-to-PDE bridge (NS-regular QOU).
